channel.title: The Seax: Essex news, sport and life
channel.description: The latest Essex news, sport and life, updated through the day.

image.title: The Seax: Essex news, sport and life

item.title: Essex urgent treatment centres under review
item.description: NHS Essex wants to hear where people go when they need help fast. Its survey will shape a new plan for urgent care.

item.title: Harlow man, 41, sent to crown court on strangulation charge
item.description: A Harlow man has been charged over an alleged offence in the town on 7 November. He is on bail until a crown court hearing.

item.title: Essex gets £1.1m to tackle stalking
item.description: Stalkers across Essex will be offered help to change their behaviour. Victims get more specialist support, including help with online tracking.

item.title: Stansted Airport Poppy Appeal raises record £26,190
item.description: Passengers and staff at Stansted gave more than ever to this year's Poppy Appeal. The total beat last year's record by over £2,000.

item.title: Southend crash: police seek dashcam footage after man seriously hurt
item.description: A pedestrian in his 40s was hit by a car in Sutton Road last Saturday. Police want witnesses and footage.

item.title: Harwich Town Council plans to digitise its Guildhall archive
item.description: Harwich's Guildhall holds thousands of historic papers, some from the late 1200s. The town council wants to start putting them online.

item.title: Lakeside gets bigger Superdry and new perfume shop before Christmas
item.description: West Thurrock's Lakeside Shopping Centre is adding shops and festive events. Superdry has moved to a larger unit opposite Boots.

item.title: Southend Sea Life Adventure wins appeal to keep wider entrance canopy
item.description: A planning inspector has overruled Southend councillors over the seafront attraction's canopy. They said it narrowed the pavement for disabled people.

item.title: Grays Town Park cafe could close over £8,000 Thurrock Council rent
item.description: Volunteers have run the Grays park cafe rent-free since it opened. Now Thurrock Council wants a yearly rent they say they cannot afford.

item.title: Essex's Prodigy star Keith Flint honoured with fossil snail name
item.description: Scientists have named a 99-million-year-old snail after the late Prodigy singer. Its hairy shell reminded them of his famous spiky hair.

item.title: Basildon end-terrace house destroyed by fire as crews protect neighbours
item.description: An end-terrace house in Basildon was completely alight when firefighters arrived. Smoke spread to the home next door.

item.title: Southend United legend Frankie Banks given Freedom of the City
item.description: The former Shrimpers full-back started the club's community work in 1991. The club says his impact goes far beyond the pitch.

item.title: Harlow Council tells government to drop asylum plan for private homes
item.description: The Home Office's contractor wants to rent homes across Harlow for asylum seekers. The council's leader wants the plan dropped.

item.title: Chelmsford murder trial: boy, 17, tells jury he carried knife for protection
item.description: A teenager accused of murdering Radwan Shakur in Central Park has given evidence. He denies being part of any turf war.

item.title: Weeley and Little Clacton bypasses to shut for four nights from 7 December
item.description: Drivers heading to and from Clacton face overnight closures on two bypasses. The road is being resurfaced.

item.title: Saffron Walden Museum catalogue goes online with 60,000 records
item.description: Anyone can now browse the town museum's collection records from home, the Saffron Walden Reporter reported.

item.title: Colchester man admits 10 thefts from garage he was banned from
item.description: Danny Archer, 40, took £550 of meat and other food from the BP in Ipswich Road. He has been remanded in custody.

item.title: Navestock fly-tippers targeted by Brentwood police van checks
item.description: Police and council officers are patrolling Brentwood's country lanes and stopping vans. The borough sees about three fly-tips a day.

item.title: Leigh police stop finds £1m of cocaine as driver is jailed
item.description: Officers found 8kg in a car boot, then 7kg more in a Southend storage unit. Douglas Kramer got six years and eight months.

item.title: Essex farmers raise fly-tipping costs at first county roundtable
item.description: Farmers told Essex County Council that rural crime and the cost of clearing dumped waste hurt them. More meetings are planned.

item.title: c2c gets £2m plan to fix delays
item.description: Rail bosses are spending more to fix the Southend line after months of delays. Some December trains will finish early or be replaced by buses.

item.title: Thurrock Council says no decision yet on selling 70 acres of open space
item.description: Three sites in Linford, Tilbury and Corringham could be sold. Residents have until 27 November to object, and cabinet would have the final say.

item.title: Essex GP surgeries to offer 32,000 extra appointments this winter
item.description: NHS Essex is paying for 8,000 more GP appointments a month until February. It is part of a county-wide plan for the busiest season.

item.title: Chelmsford parents back Havens Hospices appeal after baby son's care
item.description: Michael and Sarah Fragnito's son Elio spent his last two days at the Little Havens children's hospice. They now support its Christmas appeal.

item.title: Thurrock CVS invites would-be volunteers to drop in after Tilbury winter event
item.description: Thurrock CVS says anyone curious about volunteering can get in touch. Its co-ordinator met many residents at a busy Tilbury winter event.

item.title: Rayleigh shoplifter jailed for five months after BP garage thefts
item.description: Stefan Jaworski, 44, stole £260 of meat, fish, chocolate and alcohol. A court order bans him from every BP in England and Wales.

item.title: Southend signs 12-month contract for enviro-crime crackdown officers
item.description: Extra enforcement officers will target dog fouling and littering in Southend town centre.

item.title: Tendring Local Plan with 18,173 homes heads to government inspector
item.description: Tendring District Council will send its blueprint for growth to the government by the end of December. Public hearings are expected in 2027.

item.title: Harlow G4S cash depot workers vote to strike before Christmas
item.description: Staff who move cash for banks and shops from Harlow have rejected a 1% pay offer. A walkout could hit cash machines.

item.title: Essex this weekend: light trails, Christmas markets and switch-ons
item.description: Most towns have something festive on from Friday to Sunday. Many of the events are free.

item.title: Essex patrols targeting predatory behaviour made 128 arrests in a year
item.description: The figures come as the force marks 16 Days of Activism. Its chief constable says tackling violence against women matters every day.

item.title: Southend Airport gets easyJet flights to Corfu from May
item.description: Holidaymakers in south Essex will be able to fly direct to the Greek island next summer. Tickets are already on sale.

item.title: Cocaine kingpin who sent couriers to Harwich and Southend jailed for 18 years
item.description: Bradley Stainer ran a network that moved more than a tonne of cocaine. His couriers were paid more than £1,000 a day.

item.title: Chelmsford Local Plan hearings finish, with final day cancelled
item.description: Public hearings on Chelmsford's plan for future homes and jobs have ended. Inspectors will now decide what changes it needs.

item.title: Saffron Walden's Christmas Memory Tree invites messages for loved ones
item.description: Wooden decorations for the town's Memory Tree cost a suggested £2. The money goes to the mayor's three chosen charities.

item.title: Brentwood Civic Awards open for nominations
item.description: Brentwood Borough Council wants names of people and groups who make a difference locally. Nominations close in February.

item.title: Southend's Cliffs Pavilion unveils new foyer, bars and restaurant
item.description: The Westcliff theatre's first big makeover since the 1990s is finished. Government levelling up money helped pay for it.

item.title: Great Waltham concert to fund generators for Ukraine's winter
item.description: Ukrainian accordionist Igor Saienko plays the village church on 9 December. Entry is free, with donations going to a Felsted charity which helps fund generators for Ukraine.

item.title: Leigh Broadway's Greggs opens despite residents' petition
item.description: The bakery chain has opened on Leigh-on-Sea's Broadway. Nearly 2,000 people had signed a petition against it.

item.title: Southend's Lazydays adds Ella Eyre, KT Tunstall and Pixie Lott for 2027
item.description: Sigala, Daniel Bedingfield and Celebrity Traitors winner Bash Croft are also on the biggest line-up announcement yet for the Priory Park festival, which returns in July 2027.

item.title: Greater Anglia to give unclaimed lost property to Essex women's refuges
item.description: Refuges across Essex can now ask Greater Anglia for items left on its trains. Deliveries go through lockers to keep refuge addresses secret.

item.title: Brightlingsea's Queen Street to shut for two days from 13 January
item.description: Openreach needs the Brightlingsea road shut to lay cables. Essex Highways has issued the closure order.

item.title: South Essex crisis team uses charity kit to keep older patients at home
item.description: A south Essex NHS crisis team has bought puzzles, music and craft kits with charity money. They help older patients stay out of hospital.

item.title: Castle Point MP takes Green Belt housing worries to the Commons
item.description: Dame Rebecca Harris leads a Commons debate on housing targets and Castle Point's Green Belt. A government minister normally replies.

item.title: Air ambulance charity to study how to cut Essex road deaths
item.description: Essex & Herts Air Ambulance will study Essex crash data to learn how more lives could be saved. Road safety money is paying for it.

item.title: Essex steel firm fined £12,000 over false papers for Chelmsford gas platform
item.description: An Essex steel company supplied false safety paperwork for a platform holding up a Chelmsford gas main. It has been fined and must pay costs.

item.title: Harlow vigil reads out names of women killed this year
item.description: People gathered in Harlow town centre to remember women killed across the UK in 2026.

item.title: Witham bus link to Broomfield Hospital starts year-long trial
item.description: Witham patients and visitors get a direct bus to Broomfield Hospital from Monday 30 November. It runs on demand for a 12-month trial.

item.title: Stanway roundabout works bring more road closures into December
item.description: Closures for the new Fiveways roundabout in Stanway run into December. Peartree Road and London Road are next.

item.title: Braintree plans £7m for leisure centres and £600,000 on homelessness
item.description: Braintree's first budget plans for 2027-28 promise no cuts to services. A gap of £542,000 still has to be closed.

item.title: Maldon drafts guide to curb dust and noise from building sites
item.description: Councillors want builders to plan better for dust, noise and debris. A new guide goes to a committee on 3 December.

item.title: NHS agrees to face Maldon councillors over Southminster health hub
item.description: Councillors are worried about slow progress on a planned medical centre in Southminster. The local NHS has agreed to answer their questions.

item.title: Frosty start gives way to a raw, grey Friday across Essex
item.description: A cold dawn leads into one of the chilliest days of the week across Essex. Rain and milder air arrive on Saturday.

item.title: Brentwood Town beat Bowers & Pitsea 4-2 in the Velocity Cup
item.description: Bradley Sach scored twice inside ten minutes at The Arena. Brentwood are through to the fourth round.

item.title: Chelmsford gets Lifted as Lighthouse Family's Tunde hits the High Street
item.description: Tunde Baiyewu marked his 58th birthday with a surprise lunchtime gig. Choir singers posing as shoppers joined in.

item.title: Home Bargains in Waltham Abbey shuts on Christmas Eve for refit
item.description: The store at Highbridge Retail Park is due to reopen in spring 2027 after months of refurbishment work.

item.title: M25 delays ease after crash just past A127 junction near Upminster
item.description: A collision at about 6.45pm held traffic heading for Thurrock. Queues had cleared by about 7.25pm.

item.title: Witham Town win 2-0 at Takeley to climb to sixth in Isthmian North
item.description: Witham Town are now in the Isthmian North play-off places. Brightlingsea Regent had a tough night at the new leaders.

item.title: Harwich firm and University of Essex test VR for helicopter rescue crews
item.description: Psychologists worked with Air Rescue UK, which trains helicopter winch crews in Harwich, on a simulator that lets them practise emergencies too dangerous to stage for real.

item.title: Harlow police sergeant sacked over comments about a detainee
item.description: An Essex Police sergeant has been dismissed for gross misconduct. A hearing found he made derogatory remarks about someone held at Harlow Police Station.
